correctness.rationale: A self-contained exact p-adic product argument proves the prime-square single-column congruence, including x=0, p=2 and a=1. Three high input digits provide all output digits; bijective solving gives every fiber. N is a period, while N/p fails at n=0 for the second coordinate, proving minimality. Exact harmonic reflection and counting prove support and uniform marginals. Nine exhaustive integer-binomial period checks (up to 14641 indices) match the formula; no infinite claim is based on finite checking alone.

value.rationale: The naturally adjacent fixed columns are successive prime-power levels of iterated binomial primitives. Their individual p-square uniformity versus exact simultaneous exclusion of roughly half all pairs is an informative structural contrast, for every prime and exponent; the h_p-dependent count resolves the complete intrinsic joint spectrum rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
